## `HotkeyChord`

sealed class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Input.HotkeyChord` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

Implements: `IEquatable<HotkeyChord>`

One key combination, as text. Unity-free on purpose: the runtime chord is BepInEx's `KeyboardShortcut`, and this is the half of it that can be parsed, formatted and unit-tested without an engine.

It exists because the keys have to be readable. BepInEx serialises a shortcut as `"S + LeftShift + LeftControl"` (main key first, then the modifiers sorted by KeyCode value - `KeyboardShortcut.SanitizeKeys`), which is correct and unreadable; a person wants `Ctrl+Shift+S`. Both forms parse, and [`HotkeyChord.Format`](#hotkeychord--format) always produces the short one, with the modifiers in the order a person writes them.

<a id="hotkeychord--ctor"></a>

### `HotkeyChord(string mainKey, params string[] modifiers)`

Creates a chord.

**Parameters**

- `mainKey`: Unity `KeyCode` name of the key pressed last, e.g. `F9` or `S`. Null or empty means "not bound" ([`HotkeyChord.IsSet`](#hotkeychord--isset) is then false).
- `modifiers`: Unity `KeyCode` names held down first, e.g. `LeftControl`. Null entries and blanks are dropped; order is preserved.

**Parameters**

<a id="hotkeychord--format"></a>

### `string Format()`

The short, human form: `Ctrl+Shift+S`, `F9`, [`HotkeyChord.NotSetText`](#hotkeychord--notsettext) when unbound.

Modifiers are printed in the order a person writes them - Ctrl, Shift, Alt, Cmd - whatever order they arrived in. BepInEx sorts a shortcut's modifiers by KeyCode value, which puts Shift (304) before Ctrl (306), so without this the console would advertise `Shift+Ctrl+S` for the chord everyone calls Ctrl+Shift+S.

<a id="hotkeychord--tryparse"></a>

### `static bool TryParse(string text, out HotkeyChord chord)`

Parses `Ctrl+Shift+S` (modifiers first) or BepInEx's `S + LeftControl + LeftShift` (main key first). The two are told apart by the separator: BepInEx always pads its `+` with spaces, the short form never does.

**Parameters**

- `text`: The chord text. Null, empty or unparseable yields false.
- `chord`: The parsed chord; null when this returns false.

**Returns:** True when `text` named at least one key.

<a id="hotkeydebounce"></a>

## `HotkeyDebounce`

sealed class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Input.HotkeyDebounce` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

Fires a hotkey at most once per frame. Pure, so the rule can be tested without an engine.

Every function is bound to two chords (an F-key and a Mac-friendly Ctrl+Shift chord) and both are polled in the same `Update`. Without this, a user who happens to satisfy both — or a second poll in the same frame after the host was rebuilt — would run the action twice. Release detection is BepInEx's job (`KeyboardShortcut.IsDown` is `GetKeyDown`); this only collapses the same frame.

<a id="hotkeydebounce--neverfiredframe"></a>

### `const int NeverFiredFrame = -2147483648`

Frame number that means "nothing has fired yet".

<a id="hotkeydebounce--lastfiredframe"></a>

### `int LastFiredFrame { get; }`

The frame this hotkey last fired on, or [`HotkeyDebounce.NeverFiredFrame`](#hotkeydebounce--neverfiredframe).

<a id="hotkeydebounce--reset"></a>

### `void Reset()`

Forgets the last frame, so the next [`HotkeyDebounce.TryFire`](#hotkeydebounce--tryfire) always succeeds.

<a id="hotkeydebounce--tryfire"></a>

### `bool TryFire(int frame)`

Claims the right to run the action on `frame`.

**Parameters**

- `frame`: Unity's frame counter.

**Returns:** True the first time it is called for a given frame, false for any further call in the same frame. A frame number lower than the last one (a counter reset) is accepted, so a wrapped or restarted counter cannot deadlock the key.

<a id="hotkeydefaults"></a>

## `HotkeyDefaults`

static class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Input.HotkeyDefaults` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

The rule that decides whether a `[Keys]` entry a user already has on disk should be rewritten to a new default pair. Pure, so the one destructive thing the key registry does to an existing config file can be unit-tested without an engine.

The chord is the primary chord on macOS and Windows (`Ctrl+Shift+S | F9` instead of `F9 | Ctrl+Shift+S`), because on macOS an F-key is a media key unless Fn is held and both platforms should read the same. A .cfg written by an older build still holds the old pair, and BepInEx never revisits a value it has already bound - so the framework migrates exactly one case: the entry is still, verbatim, the pair the old build wrote. Anything else is a choice the user made, and is left alone.

<a id="hotkeydefaults--migratedlinesuffix"></a>

### `const string MigratedLineSuffix = " to chord-first defaults"`

What the registry logs when it rewrites a pair, e.g. `KEYS: migrated smoke.run to chord-first defaults`.

<a id="hotkeydefaults--ispair"></a>

### `static bool IsPair(HotkeyChord primary, HotkeyChord alternate, HotkeyChord expectedPrimary, HotkeyChord expectedAlternate)`

True when two chords are the same two chords, in the same roles.

**Parameters**

- `primary`: The primary chord to compare.
- `alternate`: The alternate chord to compare.
- `expectedPrimary`: The primary chord expected.
- `expectedAlternate`: The alternate chord expected.

<a id="hotkeydefaults--migratedline"></a>

### `static string MigratedLine(string id)`

The line the registry logs after a rewrite.

**Parameters**

- `id`: Registry id of the migrated key, e.g. `smoke.run`.

<a id="hotkeydefaults--shouldmigrate"></a>

### `static bool ShouldMigrate(HotkeyChord storedPrimary, HotkeyChord storedAlternate, HotkeyChord oldPrimary, HotkeyChord oldAlternate, HotkeyChord newPrimary, HotkeyChord newAlternate)`

Whether the stored pair should be replaced by the new default pair.

**Parameters**

- `storedPrimary`: The `<id>.Primary` value read from the config file.
- `storedAlternate`: The `<id>.Alt` value read from the config file.
- `oldPrimary`: What this build's predecessor used as the primary default.
- `oldAlternate`: What this build's predecessor used as the alternate default.
- `newPrimary`: This build's primary default.
- `newAlternate`: This build's alternate default.

**Returns:** True only when every chord is known, the old pair is not already the new pair, and the stored pair is exactly the old pair. A user who changed either chord keeps both.

<a id="textentryguard"></a>

## `TextEntryGuard`

static class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Input.TextEntryGuard` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

Decides whether the control that currently has keyboard focus is a text field, so a hotkey never fires while the user is typing a note, a todo or a profile name.

The decision is made on type *names* rather than types: the framework core must not reference TextMeshPro, and the same rule has to cover both `UnityEngine.UI.InputField` and `TMPro.TMP_InputField` (the game uses the latter). The caller reads the components off `EventSystem.current.currentSelectedGameObject` and passes their type names here.

<a id="textentryguard--inputfieldsuffix"></a>

### `const string InputFieldSuffix = "InputField"`

Every type whose simple name ends in this is treated as text entry.

<a id="textentryguard--istextentry"></a>

### `static bool IsTextEntry(IEnumerable<string> componentTypeNames)`

True when any of the focused control's components accepts typed text.

**Parameters**

- `componentTypeNames`: Type names of the components on the focused object; null means none.

<a id="textentryguard--istextentrytype"></a>

### `static bool IsTextEntryType(string typeName)`

True when a component of this type accepts typed text.

**Parameters**

- `typeName`: Simple or fully-qualified type name, e.g. `TMP_InputField` or `TMPro.TMP_InputField`. Null or empty is not text entry.
